\section[o boxe]{o boxe — boxing}

\label{lesson:PT-C514-boxe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to compete, then the Portuguese for stopwatch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o boxe}
\textbf{o boxe} — \textquotedblleft{}boxing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele treina boxe no ginásio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He trains in boxing at the gym.}
\end{quote}

A boxer is \emph{um pugilista}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{boxe} is usually traced, through French \emph{boxe}, to English \emph{box} \textquotedblleft{}to hit with the fist\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o boxe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o boxe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o boxe}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to compete, then the Portuguese for stopwatch, then say \emph{o boxe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o boxe mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Boxing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[o ringue]{o ringue — (boxing) ring}

\label{lesson:PT-C514-ringue}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for stopwatch, then the Portuguese for boxing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o ringue}
\textbf{o ringue} — \textquotedblleft{}(boxing) ring\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os dois lutadores subiram ao ringue.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The two fighters climbed into the ring.}
\end{quote}

Spelled the Portuguese way: \emph{ringue}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ringue} was borrowed from English \emph{ring} (EtymDB), an old Germanic word for a circle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a espada]{a espada — sword}

\label{lesson:PT-C514-espada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for boxing, then the Portuguese for (boxing) ring.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a espada}
\textbf{a espada} — \textquotedblleft{}sword\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No museu há uma espada muito antiga.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In the museum there is a very old sword.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Espadas} is also a suit in a pack of cards: spades.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{espada} is inherited, through Old Portuguese \emph{espada} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{spatha} \textquotedblleft{}a broad two-edged sword\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), which was taken from Greek \emph{spáthē} \textquotedblleft{}a broad blade\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o judo]{o judo — judo}

\label{lesson:PT-C514-judo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for (boxing) ring, then the Portuguese for sword.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o judo}
\textbf{o judo} — \textquotedblleft{}judo\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A minha filha anda no judo há três anos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My daughter has been doing judo for three years.}
\end{quote}

In Brazil: \emph{o judô}. \emph{Andar no judo} — to do judo regularly.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{judo} was borrowed from Japanese \emph{jūdō} \textquotedblleft{}the gentle way\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o judo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for (boxing) ring, then the Portuguese for sword, then say \emph{o judo} again
\end{itemize}

\section[a esgrima]{a esgrima — fencing}

\label{lesson:PT-C514-esgrima}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for sword, then the Portuguese for judo.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a esgrima}
\textbf{a esgrima} — \textquotedblleft{}fencing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na esgrima, os atletas usam uma máscara.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In fencing, the athletes wear a mask.}
\end{quote}

The sport with swords.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{esgrima} comes from Old Italian \emph{scrima} (EtymDB), which is usually traced to a Germanic verb meaning \textquotedblleft{}to protect\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\label{lesson:PT-R514-revisao-507-514}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item skateboard, to skate, skates, (long) walk, mountaineering
  \item referee, whistle, to blow the whistle, stand, substitute
  \item goal, penalty, forward, to shoot, to head
  \item to draw, draw, opponent, to defeat, to knock out
  \item tournament, cup, medal, podium, record
  \item sports hall, basketball, handball, volleyball, gymnastics

\end{itemize}

Skateboard? (\textbf{o skate}.) To skate? (\textbf{patinar}.) Skates? (\textbf{os patins}.) (long) walk? (\textbf{a caminhada}.) Mountaineering? (\textbf{o alpinismo}.) Referee? (\textbf{o árbitro}.) Whistle? (\textbf{o apito}.) To blow the whistle? (\textbf{apitar}.) Stand? (\textbf{a bancada}.) Substitute? (\textbf{o suplente}.) Goal? (\textbf{a baliza}.) Penalty? (\textbf{o penálti}.) Forward? (\textbf{o avançado}.) To shoot? (\textbf{rematar}.) To head? (\textbf{cabecear}.) To draw? (\textbf{empatar}.) Draw? (\textbf{o empate}.) Opponent? (\textbf{o adversário}.) To defeat? (\textbf{derrotar}.) To knock out? (\textbf{eliminar}.) Tournament? (\textbf{o torneio}.) Cup? (\textbf{a taça}.) Medal? (\textbf{a medalha}.) Podium? (\textbf{o pódio}.) Record? (\textbf{o recorde}.) Sports hall? (\textbf{o pavilhão}.) Basketball? (\textbf{o basquetebol}.) Handball? (\textbf{o andebol}.) Volleyball? (\textbf{o voleibol}.) Gymnastics? (\textbf{a ginástica}.) Marathon? (\textbf{a maratona}.) Athletics? (\textbf{o atletismo}.) Cycling? (\textbf{o ciclismo}.) To compete? (\textbf{competir}.) Stopwatch? (\textbf{o cronómetro}.) Boxing? (\textbf{o boxe}.) (boxing) ring? (\textbf{o ringue}.) Sword? (\textbf{a espada}.) Judo? (\textbf{o judo}.) Fencing? (\textbf{a esgrima}.)
